description:
Joaninha is a family team from Brazil formed by four members with different ages and creative skills. 

We are beginners in space technology and software development.
summary: JOANINHA is a cozy 2D pixel-art game about planning a Moon mission, designed for one to four players. A floating ladybug companion explains each decision and cheers the crew on, but never decides for them. Players learn that every space design choice has a cost in mass, power and points. Our current prototype is unfinished: it has a menu, a loading screen, a lunar scene, a walking astronaut and the companion that follows. The mission systems are designed and still being built
details:
What it does. The player explores the lunar surface as an astronaut with Joaninha, a ladybug companion. The full design adds a hangar where players build a spacecraft, spend points like money, buy food and fuel, and then face Mission 1, “The Long Lunar Night”. The lunar night lasts about 14 Earth days.

Benefits. Players learn by choosing. Battery, heater and antenna cost points and mass, and the consequences are visible. The game is friendly and funny, so it works for people who find space engineering intimidating.

Intended impact. We want to make space mission design feel approachable and encourage teamwork. Up to four players share one screen with roles (Command, Engineering, Science, Communications). Each new mission unlocks only after the team answers a question about what they learned.

Tools. Godot 4, GDScript and hand-drawn pixel art.

Creative aspect. The ladybug is the guide and the emotional center of the game. The tone is warm and humorous.

Factors we considered. Scientific accuracy (real NASA sources, with fictional game numbers clearly labeled), accessibility for beginners, and a scope that fits the time we had.

NASA data. We used these sources as scientific foundation:

  • NASA NTRS, “A preliminary tidal analysis of TOPEX/POSEIDON altimetry”: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19950049123
  • NASA Goddard, “Tidal Spherical Harmonics”: https://core2.gsfc.nasa.gov/ggfc/tides/harmonics.html
  • NASA Open Data, “Harmonic Constants for Baroclinic Tide Prediction”: https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/harmonic-constants-for-baroclinic-tide-prediction

They inspired the Moon-and-ocean theme. They are not yet integrated into the prototype code.

Current status (honest note). The prototype is not complete. We ran into code problems during development, and an AI assistant helped us find and fix those bugs. Our team reviewed and tested the fixes. The idea, design, story and pixel art are ours. No AI runs inside the game. Game values are fictional.
